core.title: A small wagon can still be mis-cut: MERGE or SPLIT
core.given: A wagon cut is being judged.
core.when: The wagon is densely coupled to a neighbor, or it contains two internal clusters.
core.then: The wagon can be mis-cut even if its footprint is small: densely coupled to a neighbor -> MERGE; two internal clusters -> SPLIT.
prefer: Apply the source's two patterns as stated: densely coupled to a neighbor -> MERGE; two internal clusters -> SPLIT.
avoid: Calling a wagon well-cut just because its footprint is small.
core.why: Complexity is super-linear in cross-wagon coupling, so a small wagon can still be mis-cut.
evidence: Nonbinding illustration (the source is documentation-only; this is not an acceptance requirement): a wagon's footprint alone is not cited as proof that its cut is correct.
verification: Documentation-only in the source: signals of these patterns are advisory until calibrated (per the complexity model's enforcement-posture companion rule); this rule imposes no strict check today.
The two mis-cut patterns (densely coupled to a neighbor -> MERGE; two internal clusters -> SPLIT) carry no numeric threshold in the source.

Observability scope: the change facts need a diff-level observer over the produce/consume graph, and the finding facts need the complexity model's advisory graph-proxy reporters (conservative graph proxies over the produce/consume graph) to emit findings; until those observers exist, those facts are not observable.

fires: The planner proposes splitting or merging wagons, or moving plan artifacts between wagons.
The planner judges a wagon well-sized because its footprint is small.
An advisory report flags a wagon as densely coupled to a neighbor, or as containing two internal clusters.
doesNotFire: Code edits inside a wagon that change neither its plan artifacts, its boundary, nor its produce/consume declarations.

neutralityNotes: The rule is a planning-methodology convention with no stack, runtime, framework, language, package-manager, suffix or path specifics, so almost everything carries into the core verbatim. Retained methodology terms: 'wagon' (a bounded slice of the product — the structure-profile vocabulary itself treats it as stack-independent, cf. layout.wagon_dir), MERGE/SPLIT, 'footprint', the 'produce/consume' graph, and 'graph-proxy reporters' (conservative graph proxies over the produce/consume graph) — these belong to the ATDD recompose model, not to any stack, so the graph-proxy observer context is kept in core verification. The artifact name 'WMBT' was neutralized to 'plan artifact', with the concrete kind supplied by roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The finding names (separability signal, granularity signal, coupling-complexity report) are the complexity model's advisory vocabulary and were kept in the core rather than pushed to bunOnly, since they name cross-rule methodology signals, not this realization's finding ids. The only bunOnly residue is the sibling-rule id pointer. The absence of a numeric threshold for the two mis-cut patterns is stated as a fact from the source; it does not forbid future calibrated quantitative checks.
